_README: One vocabulary of systems: the rules that turn an application (its process name) and a window title into the name of the business system the work happened in ('Salesforce', 'SAP', 'Excel', 'Outlook'). A browser is only where a web system ran, so a browser window is named by the web system its title names. Read by normalization/app_names.py (system_name, and the per-application names in stats.json meta.app_names) and by the viewer, so both name a system the same way. The rules are ORDERED and the first match wins. A rule matches when the application is one of `process` (lowercase, without '.exe') and, when the rule has a `title`, that regular expression finds a match in the window title, ignoring case (keep it plain: it runs in Python and in JavaScript). A rule without a `title` also names the application itself (meta.app_names). When no rule matches, the application's readable name is used: meta.app_names, else the executable name without '.exe', capitalized when it is all one case. A rule with `site: true` (2.0.1) names a browser window by the web system its title ends with, for a site no rule above names: the title's segments (split at a spaced hyphen, pipe, en or em dash, or '::'), a last segment that names the browser itself dropped (one of `drop`, compared without zero-width spaces), and then the last segment, 'Order Desk' in 'Customer lookup - Order Desk - Google Chrome', with an ending 'and N more pages' cut; it names nothing when fewer than two segments are left (a lone 'New Tab' is a page, not a site) or when the value rules of screen-label-patterns.json would change the segment (a value, not a name); the next rule then applies. A System the analyst sets on a step still wins. Keep it dependency-free JSON.

program_names._README: The names Windows gives a program, which the capture app records for the window in front (a live recording's Timeline bands carry 'Google Chrome', not 'chrome.exe'), each with the application (lowercase, without '.exe') the rules below know it by, so the rules apply to them too: a Chrome window on Order Desk reads 'Order Desk' on the Timeline as in the steps, and 'Microsoft Excel' reads 'Excel' (2.0.1). Compared lowercased, without zero-width spaces.
